Congress can enact legislation that contradicts an EO, and legislation wins, hands down.

Article 2, Clause 6 (emphasis added):

In Case of the Removal of the President from Office, or of his Death, Resignation, or Inability to discharge the Powers and Duties of the said Office...

That's a pretty broad term that could easily apply to not doing your job correctly. I sincerely doubt that interpretation would ever be proposed.

Local and State governments can simply choose not to follow the EO. There's not a whole lot that the president can do. Executive Orders are not an enumerated power of the president (they are not explicitly mentioned in the Constitution). There are a legally recognized application of executive authority. But, the President at no time as any authority over US Congress - quite the opposite, in fact. Further, the president has no authority over the Chief Executives of the individual states, and certainly has no authority over the legislative bodies of the individual states.

Executive Orders are executed by federal employees as a matter of obligation, by state employees as a matter of acquiescence.

The Burrows were tense. An old warrior, Sha'fu, had vanished into the night seemingly in the pursuit of some unknown foe. The alarm was raised and a search party dispatched. Though they searched for many hours there was no sign of the old drunkard, nor his unseen foe. The Med'ja-Hom however, now had a greater concern.

Though the scouts had returned empty handed they brought word of a terrible discovery; The Gods, they feared, had become angry; the once blue sky now dark, undulating with a fury the likes of which they'd never seen before. Twisting and turning, rising and falling upon itself as though it sought to consume the light which pierced its veil.

Their world was uncertain, their future dark. The tribe of the Med'ja-Hom did as they had always done during times of fear turning to their Elders for guidance and the comfort of the [songs of old](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CbY0AumIjO4).

Elsewhere....

---

Though age had dulled the old Med'ja's movements it had not dulled the keenness of his blade, Jagerite parting flesh and bone as the old warrior wrought his fury upon his foe. He had travelled for many days and many nights stopping only when exhaustion smote him down. He feared neither beast nor blade as he carved a path ever southward drawing closer and closer to the realm of his foe.

Mara, greatest of the beasts of Hom had existed since the world was made and her children had grown numerous both in size and number, their kingdom once extending far to the north where the forest met the plains. Had it not been for the bravery and sacrifice of his ancestors their tribe would surely have been sundered, his kin hearded like ants into the maw of the great beast.

Sha'fu thanked the Goddess for entrusting him with this great task, for should he succedd not only would he win her love but he would return a hero greater than any before, songs would be sung of his deeds and honor brought unto his name. So distracted was he by these thoughts that he had nary a moment to avoid a mortal blow, his foe striking down with rending claws

Sha'fu thrust upwards, his blade piercing deep into the creature's chest. A dark river of blood raining down upon him. The creature collapsed with a shudder, a wet gurgle escaping its lips as the creature breathed its last. With his foe slain Sha'fu cleaned his blade with a wipe across the creature's hide and resumed his journey south, driven ever onward by his love's siren call the chaos of the sky above unnoticed as he forged ever onward to claim his destiny.
